findings.claim: ADR-0009 says the journal's `cmd` rows (kind = shell / `ctx_execute`) and the PostToolUseFailure line are filled from the PostToolUse hook payload (TECH-SPEC GP6: 'PostToolUse payload sequence'). On Claude Code, PostToolUse never fires for the plugin's own MCP tools. `ctx_execute`, `ctx_search`, `ctx_fetch_and_index` and `ctx_index` ARE the plugin's own tools, so any `cmd` or `index` journal row that depends on this hook path will never be written for them, and the 'open errors' section of the compaction state will never show a failed `ctx_execute` call.
findings.evidence: v1 commit 320ed3e5 (fix(forward): bridge ctx_search/ctx_fetch retrieval bytes to the platform), commit message: 'Root cause: PostToolUse never fires for the plugin's OWN MCP tools, so the hook-side extractMcpToolCall path never observes ctx_search / ctx_fetch_and_index... This is a server-emit fix, not a hook-extract fix: releasing the existing hook-based code would NOT have populated the field, since the hook never sees these calls.' Code comment in the same diff, hooks/posttooluse.mjs: 'the hook NEVER fires for the plugin's own MCP tools, so this is the only place that signal can enter the forward stream.' ADR-0009 line 44 names only PostToolUseFailure as the source of failure rows and does not mention this gap. TECH-SPEC.md:294 GP6 ties the journal test to 'PostToolUse payload sequence'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 320ed3e5 2026-06-26 fix(forward): bridge ctx_search/ctx_fetch retrieval bytes to the platform. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'bytes_retrieved was 0 across all 124,454 prod events... Root cause: PostToolUse never fires for the plugin's OWN MCP tools.' The v1 fix was a tmp-file marker written by the SERVER and consumed by the NEXT ordinary tool's PostToolUse hook (consume-once). REGRESSION_RISK: v2's journal design (ADR-0009 §1) assumes a uniform hook-based event source ('Claude Code also registers PostToolUseFailure. Without it, failures are never recorded.') and gives no server-side write path for the plugin's own tool calls, so it reintroduces exactly the v1 bug for `cmd`/`index` rows sourced from ctx_execute/ctx_search/ctx_fetch_and_index/ctx_index. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: journal rows for the plugin's own tools must be written by the server directly (synchronously, at the point the tool handler returns), not through the PostToolUse hook; only rows for OTHER tools (Bash, Read, Grep, Write/Edit, WebFetch) may rely on the hook. Do not resurrect the v1 tmp-marker bridge — the server already runs in-process with the same `context.db` connection used by the journal, so it can insert the row directly without a file handshake.
findings.fix: Add to ADR-0009 §1: 'Rows for context-mode's own tools (ctx_execute, ctx_search, ctx_fetch_and_index, ctx_index) are written by the MCP server directly when the tool handler returns, not via PostToolUse — Claude Code never fires PostToolUse for a server's own MCP tools (v1 #at 320ed3e5). PostToolUseFailure/PostToolUse cover every other tool.' Add a GP6 golden: a failing `ctx_execute` call appears as an open error in the next compaction state with no PostToolUse hook in the fixture.

findings.claim: DECISIONS-r3.md Q19 lists owner rulings for ADR-0008/PRD §7/ADR-0006 but does not cover the two prior agent-claude-code review findings against ADR-0016: (a) subagent detection must key on `agent_id`, not `agent_type` (the main thread of a `--agent` session also carries `agent_type` and would wrongly be treated as a subagent), and (b) the tool-set lookup must subtract `disallowedTools` and account for plugin/`--agents`-JSON sources, or a subagent with `disallowedTools: mcp__*` is misclassified as case A and gets a deny it cannot follow. ADR-0016 lines 18-19 are unchanged from the r3 version that was flagged, so these two defects are still live in the doc going into this round.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0016-subagent-context-protection.md:18 still reads 'The hook payload carries `agent_type` for tool calls made inside a subagent.' and line 19 still reads 'No `tools:` line means the agent inherits all tools, MCP included' with no mention of `disallowedTools`. docs/v2/review/out/r3/A/round1/review/agent-claude-code.json findings[0] and findings[1] raised exactly this against the identical text. docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md 'Doc changes still to do' table has no row naming ADR-0016 lines 18-19 for this fix (only Q1/Q2/Q3 touch ADR-0016, and none of them is about agent_id or disallowedTools).
findings.archaeology: Not re-run here; see the r3 agent-claude-code.json entry for the full archaeology (85f64d2c 2026-06-21, v1 hooks/pretooluse.mjs:167, #794/#832/#834). This finding is about process: the r3 fix was never queued for the doc edit, not about new facts.
findings.fix: Add an explicit row to DECISIONS-r3.md's 'Doc changes still to do' (or a new Q) that queues the agent_id/disallowedTools fix for ADR-0016 lines 18-19, so the next doc-edit pass does not drop it. Until that row exists, carry this forward as a blocker on ADR-0016, not as a resolved item.
